verdict_reason: no authoritative point-in-time tick-size source exists in any project authority, and under the frozen NO FALLBACK rule mintick therefore cannot be bound

supplements.relationship: additional binding authority; the base spec is not edited

searched.result: no tick/increment column; the only matches are the substring inside 'ticker'

searched.source: frozen project reference tables with effective dates

mintick.resolution_key: security identity AND bar timestamp, never ticker string alone
mintick.pine_binding: prevBodySafe = math.max(prevBody, syminfo.mintick), with the resolved point-in-time value and no numerical surrogate, epsilon or floor

exposure_measurement.question: how often does mintick actually bind on Massive data
exposure_measurement.method: prevBody = |prev close - prev open| over COMPLETE 15m bars with an available prior COMPLETE bar
exposure_measurement.legacy_contrast: legacy prices are stored to two decimals, so a legacy prior body is either 0 or at least $0.01; the exposure is a MASSIVE-side problem created by full precision
exposure_measurement.why_it_matters: mintick sets the denominator of bodyRatioOk, which gates fullyEngulfs, which decides T4 and T6 — ranks 1 and 2 in the priority chain, preempting every state beneath them
exposure_measurement.plain_statement: roughly one bar in seventeen would have its T label decided by a number the project cannot source
exposure_measurement.consequence_of_guessing: choosing $0.01 would silently author the outcome on ~6% of the population, and that authorship would then appear in the report as feed divergence

evidence.inference: a fixed offset cannot produce both; only UTC storage of an 09:30 ET open can. 13:30 UTC = 09:30 EDT, 14:30 UTC = 09:30 EST.

massive.convention: left-closed, left-labelled; bar_start is epoch ms UTC

timestamp_alignment.session_boundaries: the 26-bar structure holds on both sampled sessions; early-close and open/final-interval behaviour must still be verified across all sessions in smoke

evidence.reading: legacy is Massive rounded to two decimals — same basis, different precision

price_basis.corroborates: the recovery artifact's daily-level STORAGE_PRECISION_ROUNDING finding, now seen at 15m
price_basis.limitation: one security, one session, three bars — indicative only; the taxonomy PRICE_BASIS_CONFIRMED_COMPARABLE / PRICE_BASIS_DIFFERENCE / PRICE_BASIS_UNRESOLVED must be assigned by measurement in smoke

forbidden: rescaling one source to match the other
reverse-engineering split factors from price ratios
rounding Massive OHLC to legacy precision as primary input
adjusting legacy OHLC to improve label agreement

z7_internal.why_computed: recovered T semantics require prev1IsBear = (close[1] < open[1]) OR Z7_raw[1]
z7_internal.allowed: exact T dependency evaluation only; an internal diagnostic value may be retained for verifier inspection
forbidden: appearance in the research-facing feature registry

required: current-only tick metadata cannot be backfilled historically without continuity evidence
a wrong effective-dated mintick changes the boundary predicate and is detected
an ambiguous legacy timestamp convention yields HOLD
a price-basis-unresolved observation cannot be labelled pure SOURCE_FEED_OHLC_DIFFERENCE
Z7_raw cannot become research-facing Z output

decision_required.summary: mintick has no source in this project, and it decides the T label on roughly 6% of Massive bars

options.name: admit an external regulatory authority as the tick source
options.detail: US equity minimum increments are set by rule rather than by vendor metadata; adopting that as the authority would need it named, versioned and frozen like any other source
options.effect: mintick becomes resolvable and the port executes
options.note: this ADDS an authority the project has not previously used — it is a real provenance decision, not a lookup

options.name: accept UNAVAILABLE_MINTICK where it binds
options.detail: T is executable only on the ~94% of bars where prevBody is large enough that mintick cannot change prevBodySafe
options.effect: the port runs with an explicit, measured availability hole concentrated exactly on small-bodied bars
options.caveat: that hole is not random — it selects against low-volatility and low-priced bars, which is itself a population statement that must be reported

options.name: hold the port until a vendor tick source is obtained
options.effect: no T port until authoritative point-in-time increment data exists

decision_required.not_chosen_here: I am not selecting among these; each changes what the study population means
